'''''Scutellaria minor''''', the '''lesser skullcap''', is a species of [[flowering plant]] in the family [[Lamiaceae]].

==Description==
''Scutellaria minor'' grows to {{convert|25|cm}} tall, with narrowly ovate leaves arranged oppositely.<ref name="Stace">{{cite book |author=Clive A. Stace |author-link=Clive A. Stace |year=2010 |title=New Flora of the British Isles |url=https://archive.org/details/newflorabritishi00stac |url-access=limited |edition=3rd |publisher=[[Cambridge University Press]] |location=Cambridge |isbn=978-0-521-70772-5 |chapter=11. ''Scutellaria'' L. – skullcaps |pages=[https://archive.org/details/newflorabritishi00stac/page/n656 621]–511}}</ref> Flowers are borne in the [[leaf axil|axils]] of the upper leaves; they have a pinkish purple [[corolla (flower)|corolla]], {{convert|6|-|10|mm}} long.<ref name="Stace"/>

==Distribution and habitat==
''Scutellaria minor'' has a southern temperate distribution in Europe.<ref>{{cite book |title=New Atlas of the British and Irish Flora: An Atlas of the Vascular Plants of Britain, Ireland, The Isle of Man and the Channel Islands |editor=C. D. Preston, D. A. Pearman & T. D. Dines |author=K. Walker |chapter=''Scutellaria minor'' |publisher=[[Oxford University Press]] |year=2002 |isbn=978-0-19-851067-3 |url=http://www.brc.ac.uk/plantatlas/index.php?q=plant/scutellaria-minor}}</ref> It grows in wet [[heath]]s and open [[woodland]] on acidic soils. In the [[British Isles]], it is restricted to southern and western areas, extending as far north as the [[Outer Hebrides]].<ref name="Stace"/>

==Taxonomy==
''Scutellaria minor'' was [[species description|first described]] in 1762 by [[William Hudson (botanist)|William Hudson]] in his ''[[Flora Anglica]]''. [[Hybrid (biology)|Hybrids]] with ''[[Scutellaria galericulata|S. galericulata]]'', known as ''Scutellaria × hybrida'', sometimes occur where both parent species co-occur.<ref name="Stace"/>
